mainTopic: מחילה בטעות (אונאה and איילונית), then whether produce eaten from a field that was not fully sold or was mortgaged (משכנתא) counts as אבק רבית, and when a lender is removed from a mortgaged field.
overview: The amud opens with רבא's story about רב נחמן, who holds that מחילה בטעות still counts. רבא wanted to challenge him from אונאה, and רב נחמן answered with איילונית, based on a משנה in כתובות. The גמרא rejects both comparisons. The overcharged buyer never forgave at all, because he did not know. The איילונית truly gives up her rights, because she is glad to be known as a married woman. Next comes a story: an agent buys land from a woman's relatives and tells the seller, 'You and she are relatives.' רבה בר רב הונא rules that the sale never fully took hold, so the land goes back, and the produce the buyer ate is only אבק רבית, which judges do not take back. אביי asks about a lender eating the produce of a משכנתא, and the answer is the same, because no fixed profit was set, though רבינא once ruled otherwise. Then, in the name of רבא, come rules on when a lender is removed from a mortgaged field and what happens to extra produce, with a stricter rule for orphans. רב אשי argues that the lender cannot be removed without being paid, and a story begins about a case he judged involving young orphans, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבא sits before רב נחמן and wants to object
steps.stepSummary: רבא tells that he was sitting before רב נחמן and wanted to challenge him from אונאה. רב נחמן saw it coming and showed him the case of איילונית.
steps.simpleTranslation: I was sitting before רב נחמן and wanted to challenge him from אונאה. He noticed, and showed me איילונית.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא opens a short story about a conversation with רב נחמן about מחילה בטעות. This line sets up the next two moves: the challenge, then the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן had ruled that מחילה בטעות is real forgiveness. רבא planned to attack that ruling with the case of אונאה. רב נחמן guessed the question and answered it ahead of time with the case of איילונית.

keyTerms.meaning: I was sitting before him (learning from him)
to raise an objection against him
the אמורא who holds that mistaken forgiveness is valid

phrases.english: I was sitting before Rav Nachman,
phrases.notes: The speaker is רבא, telling what happened when רב נחמן said that forgiveness given by mistake still counts.

phrases.english: and I wanted to challenge him from overcharging,
and he looked at me and showed me the case of an ailonit.
phrases.notes: An איילונית is a woman who never developed physically and cannot have children.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens רבא's account about רב נחמן's view on מחילה בטעות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets the scene: רבא planned a challenge from אונאה, and רב נחמן answered with איילונית.

steps.title: The challenge from overcharging
steps.stepSummary: With אונאה, the buyer pays too much and in a sense 'forgives' the extra by mistake. Yet the law says he gets it back, so mistaken forgiveness is not forgiveness.
steps.simpleTranslation: But look at אונאה. It is forgiveness given by mistake, and it does not count as forgiveness!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out the question רבא wanted to ask: the case of אונאה seems to show that mistaken forgiveness does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a buyer overpays and later finds out, the seller must give the extra back. If mistaken forgiveness counted, the buyer's willing payment should be treated as giving up the extra. Since he gets it back, this seems to go against רב נחמן.

keyTerms.meaning: overcharging or underpaying beyond the fair market price
forgiveness given under a mistaken belief
and it is not considered forgiveness

phrases.english: But there is overcharging,
which is forgiveness given by mistake,
and it is not considered forgiveness!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the objection רבא mentioned in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's ruling that מחילה בטעות counts as forgiveness.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In אונאה the buyer gave the extra money willingly but by mistake, and the law makes the seller return it. So mistaken forgiveness seems to be invalid.

steps.title: רב נחמן's support from the ailonit
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן points to איילונית: her marriage turns out to be a mistake, yet what she gave up during it stays given up. So mistaken forgiveness does work.
steps.simpleTranslation: He looked and showed me איילונית. That is forgiveness given by mistake, and it does count as forgiveness.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now spells out רב נחמן's answer: a case where mistaken forgiveness clearly works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The איילונית let her husband use the produce of her property because she believed the marriage was valid. When the marriage turns out to be a mistake, she still cannot claim that produce back. That fits רב נחמן's view.

keyTerms.meaning: he looked closely and noticed
he showed me
a woman who never developed physically and cannot bear children

steps.confusionAlert: The phrase 'וְאוֹדֵיק, חֲזִיתַן אַיְילוֹנִית' appears twice. The first time, in step 1, is the short story. Here it introduces the full explanation of the proof. It is the same event, now explained in detail.

phrases.english: And he looked and showed me the ailonit:
Here is an ailonit, which is forgiveness given by mistake,
and it is considered forgiveness.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 2 with a case that supports רב נחמן.
steps.raayaObject: רב נחמן's view that מחילה בטעות is valid.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The case of איילונית, where rights she gave up because of a mistaken marriage stay given up.

steps.title: The משנה source about the ailonit
steps.stepSummary: The משנה in כתובות says that a ממאנת, a שניה, and an איילונית get no כתובה, no payment for פירות, no food, and no worn-out clothes.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: the girl who refuses, the woman in a secondary forbidden relationship, and the איילונית get no כתובה, no produce, no food, and no worn clothes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה that proves the איילונית case. It shows she cannot claim back the produce her husband used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key word is פירות. The husband used the produce of her property during the marriage, and she cannot demand it back even though the marriage was a mistake. That is the mistaken forgiveness that still holds.

keyTerms.meaning: as we learned in a משנה
a young girl, married off by her mother or brother, who refuses to stay married
a woman forbidden to her husband as a secondary (rabbinic) forbidden relative
produce or profits from her property that the husband used
worn-out clothing she brought into the marriage

phrases.english: As we learned: the refusing girl, the secondary relative, and the ailonit,

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לָהֶן לֹא כְּתוּבָּה וְלֹא פֵּירוֹת
phrases.english: they have no marriage contract payment and no produce,
and no food support and no worn-out clothes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the משנה behind the איילונית proof of step 3.
steps.raayaObject: That an איילונית's mistaken giving up of rights stays in force.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה כתובות: an איילונית has no claim to פירות.

steps.title: Neither case really proves anything
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says both comparisons fail. אונאה does not disprove רב נחמן, and איילונית does not support him.
steps.simpleTranslation: But that is not so. אונאה is no challenge to him, and איילונית is no support for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא steps in and rejects both sides of the exchange. The next step explains why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Neither case is really about mistaken forgiveness. So the question on רב נחמן from step 2 falls away, and so does the proof for him from steps 3-4.

keyTerms.meaning: but it is not so (a rejection of what was just said)
a refutation of him
supports him

phrases.english: But that is not so:
overcharging is not a refutation of him,
and the ailonit does not support him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects both the challenge of step 2 and the proof of steps 3-4.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Both comparisons: אונאה as a challenge and איילונית as a support.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Neither case is truly a case of מחילה בטעות. The details come in step 6.

steps.title: Why both comparisons fail
steps.stepSummary: With אונאה, the buyer never forgave anything, because he did not know he was overcharged. With איילונית, she really does give up the produce, because she is glad to be known as a married woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: אונאה is no challenge, because the buyer did not know about the overcharge, so he never forgave it. איילונית is no support, because she is happy to give it up so that she will carry the name of a married woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the rejection from step 5 one case at a time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In אונאה there was no forgiveness at all, mistaken or not, since you cannot forgive what you do not know about. In איילונית the forgiveness is not really mistaken: she gains something she wants, the status of having been married, so she would give up the produce anyway. So neither case tests whether mistaken forgiveness is valid.

keyTerms.meaning: that he should forgive it to him
she is happy with it, it suits her
the name or status of a married woman

steps.whatToRemember: The question of whether מחילה בטעות is valid stays open here. אונאה involves no forgiveness at all, since the buyer did not know. איילונית involves real forgiveness, since she gains the status of a married woman. So neither case decides the question.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how the גמרא tests proofs. Before a case can prove a rule, it must truly match the rule. A case where there is no forgiveness, or where the forgiveness is not really mistaken, cannot teach us about mistaken forgiveness.

phrases.english: Overcharging is not a refutation of him:
because he does not know that there is overcharging
that he could forgive him for it.
And the ailonit does not support him,
because she is happy that there should go out
phrases.notes: Some versions say דתיפוק (in round brackets), but the corrected wording is דניפוק (in square brackets). Both mean 'that it should go out'.

phrases.english: about her the name of a married woman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasons behind step 5's rejection.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: אונאה has no forgiveness at all, because the buyer did not know. איילונית has real, intended forgiveness, because she gains the status of a married woman.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Neither אונאה nor איילונית decides whether מחילה בטעות is valid.

steps.title: The story of the woman, her agent, and the relative who sold the land
steps.stepSummary: A woman sends a man to buy land from her relatives. The seller asks whether he can buy it back later, and the agent answers vaguely: 'You and she are relatives.'
steps.simpleTranslation: A woman told a man: 'Go buy me land from my relatives.' He went and bought it for her. The seller asked him: 'If I get money later, will you give the land back to me?' The agent answered: 'You and she are relatives.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new section by telling a real-life story. It is setting up a ruling that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key detail is the agent's answer. He does not say yes and he does not say no. He just hints that relatives can work things out between themselves. The next steps ask what this vague answer does to the sale.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman
Buy
Land, a field
Will you give back
Brothers, relatives

steps.confusionAlert: The question 'will you give it back to me?' is asked by the seller (the relative), not by the woman. He is speaking to her agent.

phrases.aramaic: הָהִיא אִיתְּתָא דַּאֲמַרָה לֵיהּ לְהָהוּא גַּבְרָא:
phrases.english: There was a certain woman who said to a certain man:
Go buy land for me from my relatives.
He went and bought it for her.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִי הָווּ לִי זוּזֵי
phrases.english: The seller said to him: If I will have money,
will you give it back to me?
He said to him: You and she are relatives.
phrases.notes: Here נַוְולָא means 'she,' the woman. The agent is hinting: 'You two are family, you'll work it out.'

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהִיא אִיתְּתָא דַּאֲמַרָה לֵיהּ לְהָהוּא גַּבְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic. The discussion of mistaken forgiveness (איילונית and אונאה) has ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up the case: the agent answered the seller's buy-back request with the vague line 'You and she are relatives.'

steps.title: The seller relied on that answer, so the sale never fully took hold
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב הונא rules that when an agent says 'You and she are relatives,' the seller trusts that he will get the land back. So he never fully decides to transfer it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר רב הונא said: Whenever someone says 'You and she are relatives,' the seller relies on it and does not fully make up his mind to transfer ownership.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר רב הונא gives the legal ruling on the story. The agent's answer means the sale was never complete.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A sale only works if the seller fully decides to let go of the item. Here the seller heard a hint that he could get the land back, and he counted on it. Because his letting go was not complete, the land goes back to him.

keyTerms.meaning: His mind relies on it; he counts on it
Fully decides and transfers ownership

steps.whyThisMatters: This ruling is the reason the land 'returns' in the next step. That is what leads to the question about the produce.

phrases.english: Rabba bar Rav Huna said:
Any time 'You and she are relatives' is said,
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets, 'said,' and some leave it out. The meaning stays the same.

phrases.english: the seller relies on it,
and does not fully decide to transfer ownership.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא: כֹּל אַתְּ וְנַוְולָא אַחֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the legal outcome of the story told in step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The words 'You and she are relatives' make the seller rely on getting the land back. So he does not fully transfer it, and the land is returned.

steps.title: The land goes back, but what about the produce she ate?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the produce the buyer ate counts as רבית קצוצה, the full Torah-level kind, which judges take back, or only אבק רבית, which they do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: The land goes back to the seller. What about the produce? Is it רבית קצוצה, which judges take back? Or is it only like אבק רבית, which judges do not take back?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that the land must be returned, the גמרא asks a follow-up question about the crops the woman ate while she held the field.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the sale did not fully go through, the deal now looks like a loan. The seller got money, and the buyer ate the field's produce in the meantime. That produce looks like payment for the use of her money, which is רבית. The question is how strong this רבית is. רבית קצוצה is forbidden by the Torah and בית דין makes the lender return it. אבק רבית is a lighter, rabbinic level, and בית דין does not force its return.

keyTerms.meaning: Produce, the crops from the field
Fixed רבית, the full Torah-level prohibition
'Dust' of רבית, a lighter rabbinic-level prohibition
Taken back by order of judges

steps.confusionAlert: Nobody here says the produce is permitted. The only question is whether בית דין forces her to give it back.

phrases.english: The land goes back; what about the produce?
Is it fixed interest
and can be taken back through judges,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִילְמָא כִּי אֲבַק רִבִּית הָווּ
phrases.english: or perhaps it is like 'dust of interest'
and cannot be taken back?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 8's ruling that the land returns, and asks about the produce.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the produce the buyer ate full Torah-level רבית קצוצה that judges take back, or only אבק רבית that judges do not take back?

steps.title: רבה בר רב הונא: it is only אבק רבית
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב הונא answers that it makes sense to treat the produce as אבק רבית, so judges do not take it back.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר רב הונא said: It makes sense that it is like אבק רבית, and judges do not take it back.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר רב הונא answers the question from step 9. The produce counts only as אבק רבית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He picks the lighter of the two options, so the produce counts only as אבק רבית. Because of that, בית דין does not force the woman to return the produce she ate. Step 13 explains why: no fixed amount of profit was ever set.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense; it stands to reason

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא: מִסְתַּבְּרָא
phrases.english: Rabba bar Rav Huna said: It makes sense
that it is like dust of interest,
and cannot be taken back through judges.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא: מִסְתַּבְּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question asked in step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The produce is אבק רבית, so judges do not take it back from the buyer.

steps.title: רבא rules the same way
steps.stepSummary: רבא agrees with רבה בר רב הונא: the produce is only אבק רבית and judges do not take it back.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא also said: It is like אבק רבית, and judges do not take it back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds that רבא gave the same ruling. This backs up the answer and closes the discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two אמוראים reach the same conclusion. Nothing new is added to the law, but the agreement makes the ruling firm: the land goes back, and the produce stays with the buyer as far as בית דין is concerned.

keyTerms.meaning: And similarly said, used when a second sage agrees

steps.whatToRemember: When an agent says 'You and she are relatives,' the seller never fully lets go, so the land returns. The produce the buyer ate is only אבק רבית, and judges do not force her to give it back.

phrases.english: And Rava said the same:
It is like dust of interest,
and cannot be taken back through judges.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Confirms step 10's answer with the agreeing opinion of רבא.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The produce counts as אבק רבית and is not taken back by judges. Both רבה בר רב הונא and רבא rule this way.

steps.title: Does the same rule apply to a mortgaged field?
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks whether the rule for the sale case (only אבק רבית) also applies to a lender who eats the produce of a field pledged for a loan.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי asked: What about a משכנתא, a field given to a lender as a pledge? In the sale case, the reason it was only אבק רבית was that no fixed amount of profit was set. Here too no fixed amount was set. Or maybe the difference matters: there it was a sale, and here it is a loan.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי takes the rule from the sale case and asks whether it carries over to a loan secured by a field.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two ways to explain the sale case. If the reason is that no fixed profit was set, then the mortgage case is the same. If the reason is that it was a sale and not a loan, then the mortgage case could be worse, because the rules of רבית are strictest with loans.

keyTerms.meaning: A field given to a lender as a pledge for a loan. The lender works it and eats its produce.
He did not fix (set) a specific amount of profit for him.
A sale
A loan

phrases.english: Abaye said to Rabba:
A mortgaged field, what is the law?
phrases.notes: He's asking about a lender who eats the produce of a field pledged to him, with no agreement allowing it.

phrases.english: There, what is the reason?
Because he did not fix a set amount for him,
here too he did not fix a set amount for him.
Or perhaps there it is a sale,
while here it is a loan?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי לְרַבָּה: מַשְׁכַּנְתָּא, מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the conclusion of step 11 and tests whether it extends to a new case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the reason for the sale-case ruling the lack of a fixed profit (which would also apply to a mortgage), or the fact that it was a sale (which would not)?

steps.title: The same reason applies, so it is the same rule
steps.stepSummary: The reason in the sale case was that no fixed profit was set, and that is true for the mortgage too.
steps.simpleTranslation: He answered him: What was the reason there? Because no fixed amount was set. Here too no fixed amount was set.
steps.whatsHappening: The answer picks the first side of אביי's question. The mortgage case is treated like the sale case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key factor is that no fixed profit was set, not whether the deal was a sale or a loan. So the produce the lender ate is only אבק רבית, and judges do not take it back from him.

keyTerms.meaning: The reason

steps.whatToRemember: Because no fixed profit was agreed on, produce eaten from a mortgaged field is treated like the sale case: only אבק רבית.

phrases.english: He said to him: There, what is the reason?
Because he did not fix a set amount for him,
here too he did not fix a set amount for him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The deciding factor is that no fixed profit was set, so a mortgage gets the same rule as the sale.

steps.title: רבינא ruled against רבה בר רב הונא
steps.stepSummary: רב פפי reports that רבינא made a lender pay back the value of the produce he ate, against the view of רבה בר רב הונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפי said: רבינא decided a real case. He calculated the produce and took it out of the lender's hands, which is not like רבה בר רב הונא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a real court ruling that went against the rule we just learned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה בר רב הונא held that the produce is only אבק רבית, so judges do not take it back. רבינא held that it must be returned, which treats it as real רבית that judges do take back.

keyTerms.meaning: Acted on it in a real case (an actual ruling)
Calculated and took out (made him return)
Produce

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with step 13. This step is not a continuation of that answer. It is a real ruling by רבינא that goes against רבה בר רב הונא.

phrases.english: Rav Pappi said:
Ravina ruled in an actual case,
and he calculated and took back the produce,
phrases.notes: He made the lender pay back the value of the produce he had eaten.

phrases.english: not in accordance with Rabba bar Rav Huna.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פַּפִּי: עֲבַד רָבִינָא עוֹבָדָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents a real ruling that goes against the view accepted in steps 10-13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבינא made the lender return the produce he ate, against רבה בר רב הונא.

steps.title: When the lender must leave the mortgaged field
steps.stepSummary: In the name of רבא: where the custom is to remove the lender, once he has eaten produce worth the loan, he is removed.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר, the son of רב יוסף, said in the name of רבא: With this kind of משכנתא, in a place where the custom is to remove the lender, once he has eaten produce worth the amount of money he lent, we remove him from the field.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement begins about a mortgage arrangement whose rule depends on local custom.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Where the custom allows the lender to be removed, the produce he eats counts as paying back the loan. So once the produce he has eaten adds up to the amount of the loan, the debt is paid and he must leave the field.

keyTerms.meaning: In a place where the custom is to remove the lender
An amount equal to the money (of the loan)
We remove him (from the field)

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that, where the custom is to remove the lender, the produce he eats is counted as paying back the loan. רב אשי will question this rule in step 18.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר מָר בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרָבָא:
phrases.english: Mar, son of Rav Yosef, said in the name of Rava:
This mortgaged field:
in a place where they remove the lender,
once he has eaten produce worth the amount of money,
we remove him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרָבָא: הָא מַשְׁכַּנְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new teaching about how mortgage arrangements work, depending on local custom.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Where the custom is to remove the lender, once he has eaten produce equal to the loan, he is removed from the field.

steps.title: If the lender ate more than the loan, the extra is not taken back
steps.stepSummary: Continuing רבא's ruling: if the lender ate produce worth more than the loan, we do not take the extra back from him. We also do not count it toward another loan.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he ate more than the loan was worth, we do not take the extra from him. We also do not move the extra over from one loan document to another.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the same ruling said in the name of רבא in step 15. It now explains what happens if the lender ate even more than the value of the loan.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 15 said the lender is removed once he has eaten produce worth the loan. Here רבא adds that anything he ate beyond that is not taken back from him. The extra is also not used to pay off a different loan written in a different document.

keyTerms.meaning: More, extra
We take it out of his hands, meaning we force him to pay it back
From one loan document to another

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the extra simply disappears for every purpose. The point is only that בית דין will not force it back, and it will not be credited against a separate loan.

phrases.english: If he ate more
we do not take it from him,
and we do not calculate from one document to another.
phrases.notes: If the borrower owes him a second loan in another document, the extra produce does not count as paying that loan.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ruling in the name of רבא from step 15 and adds what happens with extra produce.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Extra produce beyond the loan is not taken back from the lender and is not counted toward another loan.

steps.title: With orphans' fields, the lender is removed and the extra is taken back
steps.stepSummary: When the field belongs to יתומים, the lender is removed once he has eaten the value of the loan. Any extra is taken back from him and can be counted toward another loan.
steps.simpleTranslation: With orphans: once he ate the amount of the money, we remove him. If he ate more, we take it from him, and we do count it from one document to another.
steps.whatsHappening: Still in רבא's ruling, the גמרא gives the stricter rule for a field that belongs to orphans.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first part stays the same as the ordinary case: once the lender has eaten produce worth the loan, he is removed. What changes is the extra. For orphans, anything he ate beyond the loan is taken back from him, and it is counted against another loan document. The orphans' money is protected completely.

keyTerms.meaning: Orphans
The amount of the money, meaning produce equal to the loan
We remove him from the field

steps.whatToRemember: Ordinary owner: the extra is not taken back and not counted toward another loan. Orphans: the extra is taken back and is counted toward another loan.

phrases.english: And in the case of orphans,
once he ate the amount of the money, we remove him.
If he ate more, we take it from him,
and we do calculate from one document to another.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבִדְיַתְמֵי אֲכַל שִׁיעוּר זוּזֵי, מְסַלְּקִינַן לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets the orphans' case against the ordinary case in step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For orphans, the lender is removed once he has eaten the value of the loan. Extra produce is taken back and is counted toward other loans.

steps.title: רב אשי: the lender cannot be removed without being paid
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי reasons from רבא's own rule. Since extra produce is not taken back, the lender also cannot be removed without being paid, because removing him for free is the same as taking money from him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Now that you said that if he ate more we do not take it from him, then even if he ate the amount of the money, we do not remove him without money. Why? Removing him without money is the same as taking from him. It is only אבק רבית, and אבק רבית is not taken back through judges.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי argues against the first part of רבא's ruling, the part that says we remove the lender once he has eaten the value of the loan. He builds his argument from רבא's second part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If בית דין will not force the lender to pay back the extra he ate, they also cannot cancel his loan for free. Removing him without paying him would wipe out the money he lent, which is the same as collecting the produce back from him. Since eating the produce is only אבק רבית, judges cannot take it back in either form.

keyTerms.meaning: Now that you have said, used to build a new conclusion from an accepted rule
To remove (him from the field)
Taking money out of his hands
Is not taken back through judges

steps.confusionAlert: רב אשי is not saying the lender may keep the field forever. He means בית דין cannot remove him unless the borrower pays back the loan.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ties the whole topic to the rule from step 11 that אבק רבית is not taken back through judges. It shows that removing the lender for free is really a hidden way of taking the money back.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
Now that you have said
that if he ate more we do not take it from him,
phrases.notes: He is quoting רבא's rule from step 16.

phrases.english: then if he ate the amount of the money, also
we do not remove him without money.
What is the reason?
Removing him without money
is the same as taking from him.
It is only אבק רבית,
and אבק רבית is not taken back through judges.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses רבא's second rule (step 16) to reject his first rule (step 15).
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule in step 15 that the lender is removed once he has eaten the value of the loan.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Removing him for free is the same as taking the money back. That cannot be done with אבק רבית, which is exactly why the extra is not taken back.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The lender cannot be removed without being paid, because removing him for free would be taking back אבק רבית through judges.

steps.title: רב אשי judged a real case involving young orphans
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a story about a real case רב אשי judged, involving orphans who were still minors.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי acted on this in a case involving young orphans.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a story about an actual court case. It begins with רב אשי judging a case involving young orphans, and the rest continues in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Young orphans are the case where רבא's ruling was strictest. So whatever רב אשי did here will show how far his own reasoning reaches.

keyTerms.meaning: He acted on it in a real case, an actual ruling
Minors, under the age of adulthood

phrases.english: Rav Ashi acted on this in a real case
involving young orphans
